subject: Fit pathmodel without intercept for phylogenetic independent contrasts

messages.author: 7599c3b015c0ddd9
messages.subject: Fit pathmodel without intercept for phylogenetic independent contrasts
parts:
Dear list,

I am using lavaan to perform a comparative study of correlated evolution of three traits (two endogenous variables and 1 exogenous variable).
Since these variables describe traits of a set of species (rows in the dataset), but species are part of a hierarchical phylogeny (i.e. non-independent),
it is common practice to calculate phylogenetic independent contrasts prior to the analysis.
These phylogenetic independent contrasts have a mean of zero.

If I wanted to calculate a correlation between two traits, I would force the regression trough the origin:

lm(y ~ x - 1)

My question is now, how I can realize this in the pathmodel framework in the lavaan package. At the moment I got two possible solutions:

1.
mod1_ph <-
"##### regressions
y1 + y2 ~ x
##### variances and covariances
y1 ~~ y1
y2 ~~ y2
y1 ~~ y2
##### regression forced through origin
y1 + y2 + x ~ 0*1"

mod2_ph <-
"##### regressions
y1 + y2 ~ x
##### variances and covariances
y1 ~~ y1
y2 ~~ y2
y1 ~~ y2
##### regression forced through origin
y1 + y2 ~ 0*1"

mod1 <- sem(mod1_ph, data = pic_data_scaled, fixed.x=FALSE)
mod2 <- sem(mod2_ph, data = pic_data_scaled, fixed.x=TRUE)

I would like to know
1.) which of these two solutions is closest to the linear model? and
2.) if I know that the mean of the exogenous variable is zero, is it correct to set fixed.x=FALSE, and set the mean of x to zero manually.

I hope anyone can help me.

Thanks a lot,

Jörg
